descriptionChirho: An adjective meaning new, fresh, or recently made, applied broadly to things not previously existing or recently acquired. Used of a new king who did not know Joseph (Exod 1:8), new grain offerings (Lev 23:16; Num 28:26), a new house (Deut 20:5; 22:8), a newly married man (Deut 24:5), new ropes (Judg 15:13; 16:11-12), a new cart (1 Sam 6:7; 2 Sam 6:3), new gods recently arrived (Deut 32:17; Judg 5:8), new garments (Josh 9:13), a new song of praise to YHWH (Ps 33:3; 40:3; 96:1; 98:1; 144:9; 149:1; Isa 42:10), new things God declares before they spring forth (Isa 42:9; 43:19; 48:6), a new covenant (Jer 31:22, 31), new mercies every morning (Lam 3:23), and a new heart and spirit (Ezek 11:19; 18:31; 36:26). The substantivized feminine plural chadashot means 'new things' in prophetic contexts.
